blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Despite years of academic research showing how expensive executive failure is, most organisations still onboard their most senior hires remarkably poorly. The assumption is that experienced leaders do not need help; in practice, the early months of a senior role are precisely when trust is established, relationships are formed and, critically, when avoidable mistakes are made.

The most successful executive onboarding programmes treat the first ninety days as a deliberate choreography. They include structured listening tours, early wins identified before the first day, and clear expectations set on both sides. They acknowledge that although the technical challenges are usually manageable, the political ones rarely are.

Whereas mid-level onboarding focuses on systems and processes, executive onboarding focuses on context and coalitions. Who holds the informal power? Which battles have already been fought? Which assumptions does everyone share but no one has stated? Without that map, even the most capable leader can spend six months solving the wrong problem.

items.q: According to the text, why do senior hires tend to be onboarded poorly?
options: Because senior roles change too frequently
Because experienced leaders are assumed not to need help
Because academic research is rarely published
Because onboarding budgets are usually cut first
items.why: "The assumption is that experienced leaders do not need help" — é a premissa equivocada que o texto ataca.

items.q: What do the best executive onboarding programmes treat the first ninety days as?
items.why: "treat the first ninety days as a deliberate choreography" — nada de improviso.

items.q: How does executive onboarding differ from mid-level onboarding?
options: It is shorter and less structured
It focuses on context and coalitions rather than systems and processes
It relies entirely on technical training
items.why: "Whereas mid-level onboarding focuses on systems and processes, executive onboarding focuses on context and coalitions."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Trust is built in the early months of a senior role.
A seasoned executive can be trusted to navigate the first months alone.
A capable leader can still fail by solving the wrong problem.
Political challenges are often harder than technical ones.
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro contesta a ideia de que o executivo experiente se vira sozinho no começo.

items.q: The rhetorical questions in the final paragraph suggest that…
options: the decisive information is informal and often unspoken
coalitions are irrelevant to senior roles
the answers are printed in the org chart
items.why: Inferência: quem tem o poder informal e quais premissas ninguém verbalizou — é o mapa tácito que falta ao líder.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily apresentando o plano de integração de 90 dias. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, here is how I'd frame the first ninety days for our new chief commercial officer. The instinct in the room is to have her announce a strategy in week one. I'd resist that. Before she decides anything, she listens.

I've mapped roughly thirty stakeholders, and I want her to sit down with every one of them — not for a briefing, but to genuinely understand where the informal power actually sits. The org chart tells you who reports to whom; it tells you nothing about which battles have already been fought, or which assumptions everyone quietly shares.

Now, I'm not naive about early wins. She'll need one or two visible results inside the first sixty days, and we've already identified where those might come from. But an early win chosen badly can burn more trust than it builds, so we choose carefully.

My honest worry isn't the commercial side — she's outstanding at that. It's the politics. If we get the listening right, the rest tends to follow. If we skip it, even someone this capable can spend half a year solving a problem nobody actually has.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Emily want the new CCO to do BEFORE deciding anything?
options: Announce a strategy in week one
items.why: "Before she decides anything, she listens."

items.q: According to Emily, what does the org chart fail to reveal?
options: Which battles have been fought and which assumptions are shared
The size of the commercial team
items.why: "it tells you nothing about which battles have already been fought, or which assumptions everyone quietly shares."

items.q: What is Emily's view on early wins?
options: They should be avoided entirely in the first sixty days
A badly chosen one can burn more trust than it builds
They are only about commercial results
They should be announced before she starts
items.why: "an early win chosen badly can burn more trust than it builds, so we choose carefully."

items.q: What does Emily imply is the real risk for this hire?
options: That the stakeholders will refuse to meet her
That she will move too slowly
That the political side, not the commercial side, will trip her up
items.why: Inferência: "My honest worry isn't the commercial side… It's the politics."

items.q: What does Emily mean by "solving a problem nobody actually has"?
options: Fixing something that isn't the real issue
Working on too many problems at once
items.why: Inferência: sem a escuta, o líder acerta a execução mas erra o alvo — resolve algo que não é o gargalo real.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The board underestimated the most common failure mode for senior hires." A failure mode is…
options: a recurring way in which something goes wrong
items.why: Failure mode = modo de falha: o padrão típico pelo qual algo dá errado.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "In her first month she ran a ___, meeting thirty stakeholders simply to understand them."
items.why: Listening tour = rodada de escuta: encontros para entender, não para decidir.

items.q: "Real authority ran through a quiet coalition of three directors." A coalition is…
options: a reporting line on the org chart
an alliance of people acting together
items.why: Coalition = coalizão: um grupo aliado que age em conjunto.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "An ___ in the first sixty days builds credibility before it is tested."
items.why: Early win = vitória inicial: um resultado visível cedo, que gera confiança.

items.q: Informal power is best described as…
options: the size of a person's budget
the authority granted by a job title
influence that does not appear on the org chart
items.why: Informal power = poder informal: a influência real, que o organograma não mostra.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre integração de executivos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CEO still has to sign off on the ninety-day plan." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the onboarding programme across all three regions." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the listening tour, calling it a waste of time." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "She agreed on the early wins but never followed through." She…
options: failed to carry them to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A weak first meeting won't move the needle on how the team sees her." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
